paragraphs.text: # dsh-sticky-wall
A paper sticky-note wall in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar. / DeepSeek Harness 侧边栏里的纸便签墙。
中文说明 · Appearance · Install · Data
## What it does
- Adds a **sticky wall** icon to the left sidebar panel list (order 30); the wall opens in the main

column.
- **Notes look like stationery, not UI cards** — five paper stocks, three sizes, a curled co
rner, and a silhouette weighted so the sheet hangs from its fastening (`clip-path`, derived from the
note id). Sheets lean 1.5–4.2° and stack into ragged columns, not a grid. A focused note straighten

s and lifts; its controls only appear on hover or focus.
- **Fastened the way you like** — a domed t

humb tack by default, or washi tape, a bent paper clip, or nothing at all.
- **New note** — creates

a blank note, focuses it, and picks one of five colours (amber, rose, sky, mint, violet).
- **Edit i

n place** — every note is a borderless text area; typing saves on the spot.
- **Recolour** — two dro
pdowns at the bottom of each note, one for paper colour and one for ink: paper tints the sheet, ink

colours the writing (and dims the stamp and controls to match).
- **Per-note typeface and size** — t
wo small dropdowns in a note's footer pick that note's typeface (`Wall` follows the panel) and its t

ext size. A four-line note and a single word no longer have to share a look.
- **Delete in two steps
** — a non-empty note turns its bin red and asks for a second click; an empty note goes immediately.
- **Undo a delete** — a note that goes disappears from the wall, and a strip under the header puts

it back in its old slot for six seconds.
- **Take the wall with you** — the appearance panel exports
the wall to a small JSON file and imports it back. Import merges by id, so importing the same file
twice adds nothing and never overwrites a local note. The export carries your appearance settings to

o, but an import only merges notes — it will not change how your wall looks.
- **Saves itself** — th
e wall is written to the browser's `localStorage` under `dsh.sticky-wall.v1`. No save button, no ser
ver, no network request.
## Screenshots
## Appearance
The sliders button in the panel header opens an appearance panel. Paper and fastening are segmented
switches; typeface and text size are dropdowns, because seven options in a row of buttons is a guess
ing game. All four are remembered per browser:
| Paper | What it looks like |

| **Post-it** `sticky` | Saturated stock, a soft sheen, a curled corner, and the strongest lean |
|
**Ruled** `ruled` | White pad with printed rules and a red margin line; the text line-height is pinn

ed to the rule spacing so writing sits on the lines |
| **Graph** `graph` | 16px graph grid over a f

aint paper grain |
| **Kraft** `kraft` | Brown kraft board with a vertical crease and coarser grain

|
| **Printed** `print` | Butter memo pad with faint line-drawn stationery printed across the sheet,
crisp edges and no fold |
| Fastened with | |

| **Pin** `pin` | Domed thumb tack, red / blue / green / purple / brass — **the default** |
| **Tape

** `tape` | Crooked strip of washi in a colour of its own — sometimes two, at opposite corners |
| *

*Clip** `clip` | Bent wire clip hanging over the top edge |
| **None** `none` | Just the sheet |
| Ink | |
| **Black / blue / red / green / violet** | A pen colour per note, chosen from the ink dropdown in i
ts footer. Ink only changes the writing; the paper keeps its own colour. Every ink is dark enough to
read on all five stocks, and the stamp and controls dim to match it. The first entry, **Default**,
keeps each stock's own ink |
| Typeface | Stack |

| **Default** `ui` | The host UI font |
| **Hand** `hand` | `Segoe Print` → `Bradley Hand` → `Ink Fr

ee` → 楷体 → `cursive` |
| **Kai** `kai` | 楷体 / `Kaiti SC` → `STKaiti` → `BiauKai` → serif |
| **Round

** `round` | 圆体 / `Yuanti SC` → 幼圆 → `Hiragino Maru Gothic` → `Microsoft YaHei` |
| **Serif** `serif

| **Sans** `sans` | `PingFang SC` → `Microsoft Y

aHei` → `Noto Sans SC` |
| **Mono** `mono` | `ui-monospace` → `Cascadia Code` → `Consolas` → `SF Mon

` → `Noto Sans SC` |
| **Mono** `mono` | `ui-monospace` → `Cascadia Code` → `Consolas` → `SF Mono` |

### Per-note typeface and size
The panel sets the wall's default; a single note can step away from it. Two dropdowns in a note's fo
oter choose that note's typeface — `Wall` follows the panel — and its size. `S / M / L / XL` scale w
hichever typeface the note ended up with by 0.86 / 1 / 1.16 / 1.36 — so Hand at L is bigger than Mon
o at L, and every note still sits on the ruled lines of the ruled pad (that stock pins line-height t
o the rule spacing).
## Install
Search for `dsh-sticky-wall` on the Plugins / Discover page, or:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart, or refresh the page. The panel shows up in the left sidebar at order 30 (after the Con
text panel, before the MCP connector).
## Where the data lives
Notes live in the browser profile that runs the harness UI — `localStorage`, key `dsh.sticky-wall.v1
`; appearance preferences sit beside them under `dsh.sticky-wall.prefs.v1`. They are not written to
the session log, not sent to a model, and not synced between browsers or machines. Clearing site dat
a removes them, and that is the only copy.
## How it is built
Two files, no build step, no dependencies:
- `index.js` — the Host half. The bundle patch inserts one plugin row; the row itself does nothing.
- `client.js` — the browser half. It registers a `sidebar.panellist` entry for the icon and a `main`
panel keyed by the same id, registers its `en` / `zh` dictionaries with the client locale service,
and renders the wall with the React the host's module table already provides. Paper grain is a tiled
`feTurbulence` SVG in a data URI, so there is no image asset and nothing to download; paper tints u
se `color-mix` over the theme surface.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Compatibility
`engines.dsh: >=0.2.1-rc.2`. It needs the `sidebar.panellist` and `main` slots plus the client local
e service from that release. Web UI only — there is no terminal or agent-tool surface.
## Known limits
